what: Latin text, verse translation and literal prose of three Corpus Christi hymns of St Thomas Aquinas, transcribed from one public-domain printing. Read by pipeline/build_hymn_corpus.py (HYMNS[...]['source_file']). Public domain: the text itself lives here, as the vault batch files hold Adoro te and Pange lingua.

edition.title: The Hymns of the Breviary and Missal
edition.editor: Matthew Britt, O.S.B. (St. Martin's Abbey, Lacey, Wash.)
edition.copyright_page: Copyright, 1922, by Benziger Brothers. Printed in U.S.A. Imprimatur: Patrick J. Hayes, Archbishop of New York, July 18, 1922
edition.license_basis: published 1922 (US; archive.org records possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT, copyright-region US). The translators all published before 1929 and died long ago (Henry 1946, Chambers 1893, Neale 1866, Caswall 1878).

scan.copy: University of California Libraries (nrlf_ucb:GLAD-50519704), scanned 2008-09-16, 300 ppi
scan.page_images: https://archive.org/download/hymnsofbreviarym00britrich/page/n<scan page>.jpg; printed page p is scan page n(p+9) here

transcription.method: The scan's OCR text layer (_djvu.txt) was the starting point only. Every line of Latin, verse English and prose was then read against the page image and corrected by hand: the OCR has Nee for Nec, Quern for Quem, vcre, mortalcs, Deltas, loses every ligature, and capitalises Vetera (Sacris st1) where the page has vetera.
conventions: Latin exactly as printed: the ligatures æ and œ, consonantal j (major, Hujus, Ejus), capitals and punctuation. Search folds them (search_key: æ->ae, œ->oe, j->i, v->u).
The hymn's first word, set as a display capital (LAUDA, SACRIS, VERBUM), is written in title case. Britt's stanza numbers are not text.
A verse line the narrow column turned over is rejoined as one line; a word broken at the turnover is rejoined, and each is listed in its stanza's `rejoined`.
English typography as the house writes it (Pange lingua, Caswall): straight quotes and apostrophes, -- for the dash. Britt's accented -èd (Learnèd, blessèd, bestowèd) is kept: it is metrical.

The literal prose is the quoted translation only, from Britt's numbered notes, without the commentary that follows it; italics are not kept. Line-end hyphens in the prose are rejoined (jubila-tions, com-manded, neverthe-less, re-member, sub-stance, them-selves, com-panion); in-line hyphens (To-day, life-giving, co-heirs) are the page's.

lauda-sion.title: Lauda Sion Salvatorem
lauda-sion.liturgical_use: Sequence for the Feast of Corpus Christi, and throughout the octave (Britt)

en_singable: Praise, O Sion, praise thy Saviour,
Shepherd, Prince, with glad behavior,
Praise in hymn and canticle:
Sing His glory without measure,
For the merit of your Treasure
Never shall your praises fill.
stanzas.en_literal: Praise, O Sion, thy Saviour, praise thy Leader and thy Shepherd in hymns and canticles. As much as thou canst, so much darest thou, for He is above all praise, nor art thou able to praise Him enough.

en_singable: Wondrous theme of mortal singing,
Living Bread and Bread life-bringing,
Sing we on this joyful day:
At the Lord's own table given
To the twelve as Bread from Heaven,
Doubting not we firmly say.
stanzas.en_literal: To-day there is given us a special theme of praise, the Bread both living and life-giving, which, it is not to be doubted, was given to the assembly of the brethren, twelve in number, at the table of the holy Supper.

rejoined.as: life-bringing (hyphen kept: read as a compound; OPEN)

en_singable: Sing His praise with voice sonorous;
Every heart shall hear the chorus
Swell in melody sublime:
For this day the Shepherd gave us
Flesh and Blood to feed and save us,
Lasting to the end of time.
stanzas.en_literal: Let our praise be full and sounding; let the jubilations of the soul be joyous and becoming; for that solemn day is now being celebrated, on which is commemorated the first institution of this table.

en_singable: At the new King's sacred table,
The new Law's new Pasch is able
To succeed the ancient Rite:
Old to new its place hath given,
Truth has far the shadows driven,
Darkness flees before the Light.
stanzas.en_literal: At this table of the new King, the new Pasch of the New Law puts an end to the ancient Pasch. The new supplants the old, truth puts to flight the shadow, day banishes night.

en_singable: And as He hath done and planned it--
"Do this"--hear His love command it,
"For a memory of me."
Learnèd, Lord, in Thy own science,
Bread and wine, in sweet compliance,
As a Host we offer Thee.
stanzas.en_literal: What Christ did at that Supper, the same He commanded to be done in remembrance of Him. Taught by His sacred precepts, we consecrate bread and wine into the Victim of salvation.

la: Quod non capis, quod non vides,
en_singable: Thus in faith the Christian heareth:
That Christ's Flesh as bread appeareth,
And as wine His Precious Blood:
Though we feel it not nor see it,
Living Faith that doth decree it
All defects of sense makes good.
stanzas.en_literal: This is the dogma given to Christians, that bread is changed into Flesh and wine into Blood. What thou dost not understand, what thou dost not see, a lively faith confirms in a supernatural manner.

en_singable: Lo! beneath the species dual
(Signs not things), is hid a jewel
Far beyond creation's reach!
Though His Flesh as food abideth,
And His Blood as drink--He hideth
Undivided under each.
stanzas.en_literal: Under different species (different) in externals (signis) only, and not in reality (rebus), wondrous substances lie hidden. Flesh is food, Blood is drink: nevertheless Christ remains entire under each species.

en_singable: Whoso eateth It can never
Break the Body, rend or sever;
Christ entire our hearts doth fill:
Thousands eat the Bread of Heaven,
Yet as much to one is given:
Christ, though eaten, bideth still.
stanzas.en_literal: By the recipient the whole (Christ) is received; He is neither cut, broken, nor divided. One receives Him; a thousand receive Him: as much as the thousand receive, so much does the one receive; though eaten He is not diminished.

en_singable: Good and bad, they come to greet Him:
Unto life the former eat Him,
And the latter unto death;
These find death and those find heaven;
See, from the same life-seed given,
How the harvest differeth!
stanzas.en_literal: The good receive Him, the bad receive Him, but with what unequal consequences of life or death. It is death to the unworthy, life to the worthy: behold then of a like reception, how unlike may be the result!

en_singable: When at last the Bread is broken,
Doubt not what the Lord hath spoken:
In each part the same love-token,
The same Christ, our hearts adore:
For no power the Thing divideth--
'Tis the symbols He provideth,
While the Saviour still abideth
Undiminished as before.
stanzas.en_literal: When the Sacrament is broken, doubt not, but remember, that there is just as much hidden in a fragment, as there is in the whole. There is no division of the substance, only a breaking of the species takes place, by which neither the state nor stature of the substance signified is diminished.

en_singable: Hail, angelic Bread of Heaven,
Now the pilgrim's hoping-leaven,
Yea, the Bread to children given
That to dogs must not be thrown:
In the figures contemplated,
'Twas with Isaac immolated,
By the Lamb 'twas antedated,
In the Manna it was known.
stanzas.en_literal: Lo, the Bread of Angels is made the food of earthly pilgrims: truly it is the Bread of children, let it not be cast to dogs. It was prefigured in types,--when Isaac was immolated, when the Paschal Lamb was sacrificed, when Manna was given to the fathers.

la: Tu qui cuncta scis et vales:
en_singable: O Good Shepherd, still confessing
Love, in spite of our transgressing,--
Here Thy blessèd Food possessing,
Make us share Thine every blessing
In the land of life and love:
Thou, whose power hath all completed
And Thy Flesh as Food hath meted,
Make us, at Thy table seated,
By Thy Saints, as friends be greeted,
In Thy paradise above.
stanzas.en_literal: O Good Shepherd, True Bread, O Jesus, have mercy on us: feed us and protect us: make us see good things in the land of the living. Thou who knowest all things and canst do all things, who here feedest us mortals, make us there be Thy guests, the co-heirs, and companions of the heavenly citizens.

sacris-solemniis.title: Sacris solemniis juncta sint gaudia
sacris-solemniis.meter: Asclepiadic and Glyconic, purely accentual (Britt); each Asclepiadic line kept whole, as printed
sacris-solemniis.liturgical_use: Matins hymn for the Feast of Corpus Christi (Britt)

singable.translator: a cento based on the translation by J. D. Chambers
singable.britt_says: Translation, a cento based on the translation by J. D. Chambers

en_singable: At this our solemn Feast,
Let holy joys abound,
And from the inmost breast
Let songs of praise resound;
Let ancient rites depart,
And all be new around,
In ev'ry act and voice and heart.
stanzas.en_literal: With this sacred solemnity let our joys be blended, and from our inmost heart let praises resound; let old things depart, let all be new--hearts, words, and works.

la: Qua Christus creditur agnum et azyma
en_singable: Remember we that eve,
When, the Last Supper spread,
Christ, as we all believe,
The lamb, with leavenless bread,
Among His brethren shared,
And thus the Law obeyed,
Of old unto their sires declared.
stanzas.en_literal: Of that night, the Last Supper is recalled to mind, at which we believe that Christ gave the lamb and the leavenless bread to His brethren, according to the legal precepts given to the ancient fathers.

la: Sic totum omnibus, quod totum singulis,
en_singable: The typic lamb consumed,
The legal Feast complete,
The Lord unto the Twelve
His Body gave to eat;
The whole to all, no less
The whole to each, did mete
With His own hands, as we confess.
stanzas.en_literal: After the typic lamb, and when the meal was ended, we profess that Our Lord, with His own hands, gave His Body to His brethren; He so gave It that the whole was given to all, and the whole to each.

en_singable: He gave them, weak and frail,
His Flesh, their food to be;
On them, downcast and sad,
His Blood bestowèd He:
And thus to them He spake,
"Receive this Cup from Me,
And all of you of this partake."
stanzas.en_literal: He gave to the weak His Body as food, and He gave to the sad the cup of His Blood, saying: Receive ye the cup which I give to you, drink ye all of it.

en_singable: So He this Sacrifice
To institute did will,
And charged His priests alone
That office to fulfil:
In them He did confide:
To whom pertaineth still
To take, and to the rest divide.
stanzas.en_literal: Thus He instituted this Sacrifice (Sacrament) the administration of which He willed should be entrusted to priests alone, whom it thus behooves to receive it themselves, and to give it to others.

en_singable: Thus Angels' Bread is made
The Bread of man to-day:
The Living Bread from Heaven
With figures doth away:
O wondrous gift indeed!
The poor and lowly may
Upon their Lord and Master feed.
stanzas.en_literal: The Bread of Angels becomes the Bread of men; the Bread of Heaven puts an end to types; O wondrous thing, the poor, the servant, and the lowly, eat their Lord!

la: Sic nos tu visita, sicut te colimus:
Per tuas semitas duc nos quo tendimus,
en_singable: O Triune Deity,
To Thee we meekly pray,
So mayst Thou visit us,
As we our homage pay;
And in Thy footsteps bright
Conduct us on our way
To where Thou dwell'st in cloudless light.
stanzas.en_literal: O triune Deity, we beseech Thee, that Thou visit us, as we adore Thee; lead us by Thy ways, whither we direct our steps, to the light wherein Thou dost dwell.

verbum-supernum.title: Verbum supernum prodiens (Corpus Christi)
verbum-supernum.liturgical_use: Hymn for Lauds on the Feast of Corpus Christi (Britt). Not the Advent hymn of the same incipit (Britt no. 36).

singable.britt_says: Translation by J. M. Neale; the last two stanzas by Father Caswall

en_singable: The Heav'nly Word proceeding forth,
Yet leaving not the Father's side,
And going to His work on earth
Had reached at length life's eventide.
stanzas.en_literal: The Heavenly Word going forth, yet not leaving the right hand of His Father, went forth to His allotted work, and arrived at the evening of His life.

en_singable: By false disciple to be given
To foemen for His Blood athirst,
Himself, the Living Bread from Heaven,
He gave to His disciples first.
stanzas.en_literal: When about to be delivered over to His enemies, by a disciple, to be put to death, He first gave Himself to His disciples as the Bread of Life.

en_singable: To them He gave, in two-fold kind,
His very Flesh, His very Blood:
In love's own fulness thus designed
Of the whole man to be the food.
stanzas.en_literal: To them He gave His Flesh and His Blood under a twofold species, that He might wholly feed man, who is of a twofold nature.

en_singable: By birth, our fellow-man was He;
Our meat, while sitting at the board;
He died, our ransomer to be;
He ever reigns, our great reward.
stanzas.en_literal: By being born, He gave Himself to us as our companion; at the table, He gave Himself as our food; dying He gave Himself as our ransom; now reigning in glory He gives Himself as our reward.

en_singable: O saving Victim, opening wide
The gate of heaven to man below,
Our foes press on from every side,
Thine aid supply, Thy strength bestow.
stanzas.en_literal: O Saving Victim, that openest the gate of heaven; hostile attacks oppress us, give us strength, bring us aid.

en_singable: To Thy great Name be endless praise,
Immortal Godhead, One in Three;
O grant us endless length of days
In our true native land, with Thee.
stanzas.en_literal: Eternal glory be to the Triune God, who giveth us life without end in our native land above.
